citeAs: Zhou, J., Lu, T., Mishra, S., Brahma, S., Basu, S., Luan, Y., Zhou, D., & Hou, L. (2023). Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models.
creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou (Google; Yale University)
description: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval) is a benchmark for evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models using prompts containing verifiable instructions. It includes 25 types of verifiable instructions and 541 prompts, enabling automatic and reproducible evaluation of whether model responses follow instructions.
name: IFEval
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzes annotation quality by discussing false negatives in strict verification and introducing a loose verification criterion with eight transformations to reduce false negatives, while noting that this may introduce false positives.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Instruction following is annotated automatically by deterministic verification functions for each verifiable instruction. The paper defines strict verification with isfollowed(resp, inst) and also a loose criterion using eight response transformations, including removing markdown font modifiers, removing the first line, removing the last line, and combinations of these transformations.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly positions IFEval as an easy-to-reproduce, unbiased, and automatic approach, motivated by concerns that human evaluations introduce biases and inconsistencies and model-based evaluation can be biased by evaluator model limitations.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by creating a list of 25 verifiable instructions and synthesizing prompts through four steps: generating base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions, using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts, rephrasing prompts with another few-shot prompting approach, and manually checking and editing the rephrased prompts one by one.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source data consists of base prompts and a list of 25 verifiable instructions, which were combined to create prompts. The released benchmark contains 541 prompts, each with one or multiple verifiable instructions.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically, and there are edge cases where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed. The loose verification criterion can reduce false negatives but may introduce false positives.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each prompt was constructed by appending one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions to a base prompt; prompts were then rephrased to increase diversity of phrasing.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors used few-shot prompting to identify illogical prompts and remove them, used another few-shot prompting approach to rephrase prompts to increase phrasing diversity, and then manually checked and edited the rephrased prompts one by one.
rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is intended to evaluate the instruction-following ability of large language models, compare different models on various instruction types, and analyze which types of instructions are not usually followed.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Few-shot prompting was used to identify illogical prompts and remove them, and another few-shot prompting approach was used to rephrase prompts.
